sentences.text: 4. The prosecution case is based on a written information submitted by the victim (PW 4), who alleged that, on 11.09.2022, at about 12:00 noon, when she had been going to defecate towards the agricultural field, in the meantime, the appellant came from behind, gagged her mouth and took her in the bushes nearby and then established physical relationship with her.
He also threatened her that if she would disclose it to anyone, then her parents would be killed.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that although the written information giving rise to the first information report was given on 11.09.2022, the said FIR reached the court of learned jurisdictional Judge only on Patna High Court CR.

Learned counsel further submits that in this case the police could not verify the age of the victim from the school where she claimed to have study up to class 5 and no age proof document was collected by the IO, but, at a belated stage, in course of trial, the prosecution brought one page of admission register, on which neither the school name is printed nor the same seems to be the first school admission register of the victim.

The IO Priyanka Kumari (PW 7) has clearly stated in her deposition that at the time of taking over the charge of investigation, the S.H.O. had not given her any certificate with regard to the age of the victim and she has further stated that in course of investigation she could not obtain any document relating to the age of the victim, but she had got conducted her medical examination in which the doctor opined that she was between 18-19 years of age.

7. Learned counsel further submits that one school leaving certificate (Exhibit7/1) has been brought on record again at a belated stage, which would not be called in the category of the documents as envisaged under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

sentences.text:
The Headmaster of the Primary School, Parariya (PW 8) has stated Patna High Court CR. APP (DB)
No.1083 of 2024(11) dt.25-02-2026 that the date of birth of the victim is 15.03.2006, but the defence suggested and it may be seen from the naked eyes that in column no. 6 of the said page there are over writings.
He has also stated that he had mentioned the date of birth as told by her parents and he had no certificate of the birth of the victim at the time of admission.
It is further submitted that the documents brought at the belated stage would not inspire confidence of the Court.

8. Learned counsel further submits that there is no seizure report of the clothes of the victim and from the FSL report it would appear that the clothes of the victim was sent to the FSL only on 10.10.2022 and the Assistant Director FSL (PW 9) received it on 14.10.2022, whereas occurrence is dated 11.09.2022.
the IO (PW 7) has stated that she had not collected the clothes of the victim.
In these circumstances, a mere opinion of the FSL that blood has been detected at place in the exhibit marked 'B' does not connect the appellant with the alleged occurrence.

sentences.text: Learned counsel has placed before this Court the evidence of the prosecution witnesses including the victim saying that the place of occurrence is said to be at a distance of one hour from the house of the victim.

dt.25-02-2026 that the victim would go to defecate in a field via the orchard of the appellant which is at a distance of one hour.
She claims that she was pulled away by the appellant by catching hold of her hairs, but there is no injury report of the victim on the record.

The Doctor (PW 2), who was posted at Sadar Hospital, Sasaram, as Medical Officer, had examined the victim, has stated that "victim was not appear before me" (there seems to be some grammatical error), no injury has been pointed out by PW 2 on the body of the victim.

10. Apart from the aforementioned submissions learned counsel has pointed out from the deposition of the defence witness (DW 1) that the victim girl was always stealing away the woods from the orchard of the appellant, on several occasions she was asked not to do so, but she used to indulge in abuse and all these facts were brought to the notice of the Gram Panchayat much before the occurrence.

On 09.08.2022, the father of the appellant had given written complaint in the Panchayat and in the said written complaint, he has expressed his apprehension that he or his family member may be falsely implicated.
The Gram Panchayat had sent a notice to the father of the victim, but he did not turn up in the Panchayat.
In this regard, the order of the panchayat dated 09.08.2022 has been Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1083 of 2024(11) dt.25-02-2026 brought on record as Exhibit D/1.
It is, thus, submitted that it a case of false implication, in which the appellant, who has remained in jail for about three years would deserve suspension of sentence and release on bail.
11. The prayer has been opposed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

It is submitted that the victim girl has supported the prosecution case and she has stated that this appellant had pulled her away to the bank of the river and there he had established physical relationship with with her.

12. Having regard to the submissions noted hereinabove and the materials, which we have prima facie gone through, at this stage, we have noticed that there is serious dispute with regard to the determination of the age of the victim, the IO had not collected any age proof and what have been brought on record through the Headmaster of the Primary School, at a belated stage, have been also questioned on account of over writing, which may be seen with the naked eyes, the Doctors have opined that the victim was aged 18-19 years, we have further noticed that, in this case, the victim claims that when she was going to defecate, then this appellant pulled her away by her hairs and established physical relationship with her, Patna High Court CR.

however, PW 2, who is Doctor, has not recorded any injury on the body, it seems highly improbable that the victim would go to a distance of one hour to defecate, in her deposition,
she has stated that she used to go to defecate at a place which goes through the orchard of the appellant, but she cannot say the distance, she has further stated that it takes one hour from the orchard and it takes also one hour from her house, she has further stated that the rasta is the agricultural field in which paddy crops were there, these are some doubtful circumstances and keeping in view the defence evidence on the record through DW 1 as also the custody of the appellant and that the appeal is not likely to be heard in near future, we grant suspension of Akash Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50509643/
